title: Learning disease-relevant relationships among individuals enables multi-disease prediction from the gut microbial abundance profiles
status: User-supplied manuscript; no DOI or publication date was provided.

method_paragraphs.224: The primary cohort comprised 4,012 individuals across six disease groups and a healthy control group: colorectal cancer, Crohn's disease, atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes, obesity, and overweight (C=7, n=4012). species relative abundance profiles were obtained from publicly available metagenomic studies, with input valuesjaij=1. The cohort was split into training, validation, and test partitions using stratified sampling to preserve group proportions. The test set comprised 799 individuals and was held fixed; training and validation sets were re-partitioned across five independent runs.
method_paragraphs.225: The independent cohort comprised 6,025 individuals across seven disease categories and a healthy control group: cancer, cardiovascular disease, digestive disease, immune disease, infectious disease, kidney disease, and metabolic disease (C = 8, n = 6025). The same framework was trained and evaluated within the independent cohort using its eight groups, with a fixed test set of 1,202 individuals.
method_paragraphs.228: We constructed functional profiles to represent the biological roles associated with each individual's species composition using existing biomedical knowledge. All functional descriptions were generated using DeepSeek-V3.2 (accessed via the deepseek API in 2025). Disease labels were excluded from individual-level inputs to the language model; the descriptions combined each individual's species composition and relative abundances with existing knowledge of microbial functions.
method_paragraphs.230: For each individual i, the kspecies=50 species with the highest relative abundance among those with aij>0 were selected to form a structured community profile:
method_paragraphs.240: A higher DG indicates that the prompts collectively span a broader range of semantic directions. Semantically diverse candidate prompts were combined and evaluated in successive rounds across combination sizes of four, three, and two prompts. Prompts were selected according to their predictive performance on the validation set. The final evolved prompt covered metabolic exchange, ecological interactions, host-barrier and immune-related processes, and substrate utilization.
